ops.title: TCC fix: VM pre-release gate skipped by user decision; live capture is the proof
ops.body:
2026-07-17: The Phase 4 VM validation (scripts/vm/scenarios/verify-appgroup-noprompt.sh, profiled+unprofiled) was SKIPPED by explicit user choice and all VM infrastructure decommissioned.

**Why skipped**: The host terminal app (Ghostty) was denied macOS Local Network access; a freshly-toggled grant doesn't reach an already-running process, so no process in this session could reach the tart guests (ARP resolved, all IP traffic dropped — hit even the stale fusekit-test VM, proving it was host-side, not the build). Rather than relaunch the session, the user chose to skip the rehearsal and rely on the **two-release live forensic capture on both Macs** as the proof (the definitive proof anyway — the VM was only a safe rehearsal).

**Decommissioned**: `tart delete ccpool-test fusekit-test`; `rm -rf /tmp/ccpool-vm /tmp/fusekit-vm` (clones + shared image cache); removed the host-installed VM provisioning profiles from ~/Library/MobileDevice + Xcode UserData. Base64 profile copies remain in yasyf/cc-pool CI secrets and /Users/yasyf/Code/.wt/profiles.

**Consequence for the release**: the first real cc-pool upgrade IS the test. R1 (does the Team-ID prefix alone suffice, or is the embedded profile load-bearing) stays unresolved by rehearsal — the profiled config ships regardless (sanctioned path), and the live capture will show whether any prompt survives and name its true service/client if so. If a prompt does survive, the fix follows the captured evidence (no more blind keying fixes).

The verify-appgroup-noprompt.sh scenario stays in the tree (bash-n + shellcheck clean, gate-committed) for a future run in a Local-Network-granted environment.
